rows.selection_reason: Existing evidence is nonexistent, so the first experiment should establish a baseline for multimodal performance. This configuration tests a balanced multimodal setup with PCA and ResNet50 encoders, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion—key design choices that isolate the impact of representation, aggregation, and fusion strategies. It provides foundational insights without overcomplicating the model, allowing future experiments to build on this baseline.

The existing evidence shows that config_001 (PCA RNA + ResNet50 image) achieves 0.5729 validation accuracy. This experiment tests whether switching to scgpt (a more advanced RNA encoder) and imagenet_vit_l (a larger image encoder) improves performance, isolating the impact of encoder choices. It maintains the same aggregation and fusion methods to focus on encoder effects, balancing exploration of key design decisions with minimal changes.

Existing evidence shows config_001 (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000+resnet50, transformer+weighted) achieves the highest accuracy. This experiment tests replacing the image encoder with imagenet_vit_l and switching aggregation from transformer to avgpool while keeping fusion as weighted. This isolates the impact of image encoder choice and aggregation method, which are critical design decisions with limited prior evidence. The experiment balances exploration of key components against exploitation of the current best configuration.

Existing evidence shows that avgpool aggregation (config_002) outperforms transformer aggregation (config_001). This experiment tests whether using scgpt RNA encoder with avgpool aggregation (config_013) maintains the high performance of config_002, isolating the effect of RNA encoder choice. It directly addresses uncertainty about whether the RNA encoder (pca_n2000 vs scgpt) impacts performance when using avgpool, a key design decision with strong prior evidence.

Existing evidence shows config_002 (pca_n2000 RNA, imagenet_vit_l image, avgpool, weighted) achieves the highest accuracy (0.635). This experiment tests whether switching to scgpt RNA encoder (while keeping other parameters identical) improves performance, isolating the impact of RNA representation. It balances exploitation of the current top-performing setup with exploration of a different encoder, avoiding multiple changes and focusing on a critical design choice.

Existing evidence shows that config_002 (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000 RNA, imagenet_vit_l image encoder, avgpool aggregation, weighted fusion) achieves the highest validation accuracy (0.635). This experiment tests whether changing the fusion method from weighted to concat (while keeping all other parameters identical) impacts performance. This isolates the effect of fusion strategy, a critical design choice, and helps determine if the current high-performing configuration's success depends on weighted fusion. It balances exploitation of the strong baseline (config_002) with exploration of a key hyperparameter.

Existing evidence shows that config_002 (pca_n2000 RNA, imagenet_vit_l image encoder, avgpool aggregation, weighted fusion) achieves the highest accuracy (0.635). This experiment tests whether changing the image encoder to resnet50, aggregation to transformer, and fusion to concat (while keeping RNA encoder as pca_n2000) impacts performance. It isolates the effect of image encoder and aggregation/fusion choices, which are critical but underexplored in previous experiments. This balances exploration of key parameters with the goal of improving accuracy.

Existing evidence shows that avgpool aggregation with weighted fusion (config_002) achieves the highest accuracy. This experiment tests whether switching to transformer aggregation (while keeping RNA/image encoders and fusion method the same) improves performance, isolating the impact of aggregation. This clarifies whether aggregation choice is critical, balancing exploitation of current top performers with exploration of key design decisions.

The existing evidence shows that config_002 (pca_n2000 RNA, imagenet_vit_l image, avgpool, weighted) achieves the highest accuracy (0.635). This experiment tests whether switching the image encoder to resnet50 (while keeping RNA encoder, aggregation, and fusion consistent) improves performance. It isolates the effect of the image encoder, a key design choice, to determine if resnet50 is better than imagenet_vit_l. This balances exploitation (building on the current top setup) and exploration (testing a critical component).

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with avgpool aggregation and weighted fusion (e.g., config_041) achieve high accuracy. This experiment tests whether replacing the RNA encoder from pca_n2000 to scvi_n200 (a different representation method) maintains performance, isolating the impact of RNA encoder choice. It balances exploration of critical design decisions while building on prior success with avgpool/weighted fusion.
